prize_parts.citation: for the development of targeted protein degradation by induced proximity, from PROTACs to the molecular-glue mechanism of thalidomide-type drugs

statement.case_for: Reading the eight opening ballots, I am moving my preferred prize to targeted protein degradation (B057). It is the only shortlisted candidate ranked by all eight members and placed first by three and top three by six. That breadth matters because it comes from members with very different backgrounds, but support alone is not my argument. Induced proximity is a genuinely new chemical mode of action: a bifunctional molecule or a glue reshapes a protein-protein interface so that the cell's ubiquitin-proteasome machinery removes a target, acting catalytically rather than by occupancy. From my own field I find the ternary-complex energetics (cooperativity, interface complementarity, linker and ligand effects) both hard and chemically rich, and that quantitative dimension is part of why I regard this as chemistry and not only pharmacology. The credited trio is coherent: Crews and Deshaies conceived and built PROTACs, and Handa's identification of cereblon as the thalidomide target explains molecular glues and a decades-old pharmacological puzzle. Independent confirmation across many laboratories is strong and clinical programmes are advanced.
statement.case_against: No degrader is yet approved as a drug, so the committee could reasonably judge the field slightly early, and the clinical argument rests on trial momentum, not on established benefit. Attribution is also genuinely crowded. Ciulli (VHL ligands and structural basis of ternary complexes), Sakamoto (first PROTAC with Crews and Deshaies), Gray, Ito and Kim all have serious claims, and a three-name limit forces a choice that will look arbitrary to some. My own opening favourite, Car-Parrinello dynamics (B037), is arguably the more mature and more cleanly attributed science, but only I ranked it, so I should not present it as a committee preference.

responses.point: Chabes ranks B057 first and stresses that cereblon as the thalidomide target explains a long-standing pharmacological puzzle, with Crews, Deshaies and Handa as the core.
responses.response: I agree that the cereblon work must be in the prize; without it the claim reduces to PROTACs alone and glues are left unattributed. In my opening I placed Ciulli in the third slot, but I now think Handa is the better choice because his contribution is a discovery that changes the mechanistic understanding of existing drugs, whereas Ciulli's is a later, if important, structural and ligand-design advance. I would resist treating the absence of an approved degrader as disqualifying, as you note; the mechanism is confirmed, and the thalidomide-class drugs already show it working in patients.

responses.point: Brzezinski ranks B054 first and B057 second, with Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli as the trio, noting that Ciulli supplied the structural and ternary-complex foundation, and that PROTACs may be slightly early.
responses.response: I share your reading of Ciulli's importance; the ternary-complex work is exactly what I find most chemically interesting, and I put him in my own opening trio. Where I differ is on the third name: leaving out Handa would leave molecular glues without a founder, and glues are the part of the field with approved drugs behind it. On timing I partly agree and would not call B057 uncontroversial, but I do not think waiting changes the credit picture, which is already settled. I also agree with you that B054 is a mature and strong second option and have listed it as my first alternative.

responses.point: Somfai ranks Pd-catalysed C-N coupling (B068) first for its generality and overwhelming practical reach, and notes three decades of confirmation.
responses.response: I rated B068 second in my own opening and agree on its quality: Buchwald and Hartwig's work is clean, mature and cleanly attributed, with the Kosugi precursor properly acknowledged. My reservation is not the science but the 2010 cross-coupling prize, which already honoured the Pd-catalysed coupling tradition, so the novelty claim has to be argued as a distinct bond-construction advance. Only three members ranked it, and two of the three made it their first choice, so it is a strong but narrow base of support. I would keep it as a serious contender if B057 stalls, but I would not make it my first choice over a new modality.

responses.point: Linke ranks B057 first because induced proximity uses the cell's non-equilibrium machinery to remove a target and explains thalidomide-type drugs, and ranks base editing (B016) second.
responses.response: Your framing of degradation as a chemical bridge exploiting a driven cellular process is persuasive, and it helps answer whether this is chemistry. I am less convinced by base editing as a second pick: the deaminase chemistry is elegant, but the 2020 CRISPR prize already recognised genome editing, and the conceptual step beyond it is narrower than for degradation. I would like us to compare B016 and B054 on that basis, since both are biomolecular-tool prizes and the committee has awarded several in recent years.

responses.point: Sparr ranks biomolecular condensates (B005) first, as a physical-chemical reframing of intracellular organisation, with Hyman, Brangwynne and Rosen.
responses.response: I accept that condensates changed how cell organisation is thought about and that the thermodynamic framing is strong. My doubt is that, unlike a molecular mechanism, it is still debated how far the phase-separation picture explains biological function in vivo, and the proposed attribution is split between experimental and theoretical contributors (Hyman, Brangwynne, Rosen, Pappu, Mittag). That makes it hard to write a sharp citation today. I do not rule it out for the future.

uncertainties: Whether the committee will accept a prize for degradation before any PROTAC drug is approved.
Which three names best represent the field: Handa versus Ciulli versus Sakamoto, Gray and Ito for the third slot.
Whether base editing (B016) and genetic code expansion (B054) are too close to recent biomolecular-tool prizes for a second such award in short order.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile for the shortlisted candidates. My documented tie to Arieh Warshel (postdoctoral EVB collaboration) concerns no shortlisted candidate, and none of the credited names appears linked to Uppsala or to my own work.
